newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian negotiators go to Egypt for talks.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian negotiators go to Egypt for talks.

text.p: Palestinian peace negotiators headed for Cairo on Sunday for talks with Egyptian officials on salvaging peacemaking with Israel.
"The visit is aimed at continuing consultations and coordination with the Egyptians," team leader Saeb Erekat told Reuters before leaving.
Erekat said he and two other negotiators would meet President Hosni Mubarak's adviser Osama el-Baz and Foreign Minister Amr Moussa in Cairo on Monday.

Egypt has recently stepped its mediation efforts between Israel and the Palestinians after efforts by the United States -- the main sponsor of the peace process -- failed to resolve a crisis over Israel's start of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
On Thursday, Egyptian envoy Osama el-Baz shuttled between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to try to resolve the impasse, but Cairo so far has not had better luck than Washington.
The Palestinians say they will only resume talks with Israel only when it stops work on the settlement construction. Netanyahu has vowed to continue building.
The Palestinian Authority cabinet said in a statement issued on Saturday:

"The Palestinian public was patient for a long time over the accelerating Israeli trespasses and violations and Netanyahu's affirmations on continuing the settlement attacks. They cannot be patient anymore."
Violence has periodically flared since the new settlement building began.

On Sunday, 15 Palestinians and two Israeli soldiers were wounded in the second straight day of clashes in the West Bank town of Hebron. At a Jerusalem demonstration, masked supporters of Arafat's Fatah faction burned Israeli and U.S. flags.

Palestinians have also been angered by a non-binding U.S. House of Representatives resolution on Tuesday calling on President Bill Clinton to affirm that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital.
Palestinians, who want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state, say Jewish settlement building in Jerusalem pre-empts final peace talks on the city's fate.
Israel vows never to cede any part of the city. It captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and, in a move unrecognised by the international community, annexed it.
